recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-12834 unless a human explicitly decides to rewrite archived historical release snapshots, which would be outside normal current-build reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-12834 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request raised against DSTU2 Observation. It asked to remove the Observation.bodySite requirements note "Knowing where the observation is made is important for tracking if multiple sites are possible" because that was only one possible reason and not the most likely one.
initial_application: The request was applied before this reconciliation in git commit 7f5590e232fecd512aa73c548d18d6b69282ad8d, whose subject references [#12834] and whose patch removes that Requirements cell from the then-authoritative Observation spreadsheet source. Later resource-source refactoring moved Observation to source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml, and the current Observation.bodySite element no longer carries a requirements value with the challenged sentence.
additional_context: Observation is an active current-build resource through source/fhir.ini. The current bodySite source is now deprecated in favor of bodyStructure and retains only the present-day definition/comment text. Repository-wide exact-phrase checks show the old Observation sentence only in archived tools/history release snapshots, not in active Observation source; those historical snapshots should not be rewritten as a current-spec fix. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches for FHIR-12834 and the exact phrase found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The published commit is an empty audit commit because the active current source already reflects the Jira resolution and the only Observation occurrences of the old sentence are historical release artifacts outside the current build source.
